{ "item": { "id": "125fc690-3b1f-4ddd-a40a-79def72082f5", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Concepts", "short_description": "The three core building blocks of Godzilla: pipelines, connectors, and events.", "body": "{{ds:component/hero|title=Concepts|subtitle=The three building blocks every Godzilla pipeline is made of.|cta_html=Start with Pipelines}}\n\n
\n

Godzilla is built from three ideas that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

\n\n {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/5ac66235-69dc-4092-b430-9d68837e0c76}}|tag=Concept|title=Pipelines|description=Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.}}\n {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/7418c3d6-9ea1-4d1c-8d8f-73136f6b6abb}}|tag=Concept|title=Connectors|description=Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.}}\n {{ds:component/card|href={{cms:item/6277e4fb-3e99-45b0-a7f6-aefe69c5778f}}|tag=Concept|title=Events|description=The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.}}\n
\n\n
\n

How they fit together

\n

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

\n

{ "item": { "id": "6277e4fb-3e99-45b0-a7f6-aefe69c5778f", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Events", "short_description": "What an event is in Godzilla: the atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.", "body": "

Events

An event is the atomic unit of data that moves through a Pipeline. Every record a source connector emits, every row a transform produces, and every write a destination connector performs is an event.

Event shape

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=event.json|language=json|code={ "id": "evt_8f2c1a90", "type": "order.created", "occurred_at": "2026-08-18T09:12:44Z", "source": "connector_postgres_orders", "payload": { "order_id": "ord_4471", "amount_cents": 4899 } }}}

User data events vs. platform events

Godzilla distinguishes two kinds of events:

  • User data events — the records your pipelines process, shaped however your source system produces them.
  • Platform events — lifecycle notifications Godzilla itself emits: pipeline.started, pipeline.completed, pipeline.failed, connector.error. These are what power Webhooks.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Ordering|body_html=

Events are delivered in-order per source partition, not globally. Two events from different source partitions may be processed out of order relative to each other.

}}

Retries and dead-lettering

An event that fails a transform or destination write is retried with exponential backoff. After the configured retry limit, it is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped. See Handling errors & retries for how to configure and drain a dead-letter queue.

", "version_token": "8b018ec8-940f-45fa-943c-65d3c8b6991b", "created_at": "2026-08-20T14:09:57.054Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-20T15:07:12.070Z", "placement_id": "a92c392b-2913-4501-8eea-6ffdff292168", "folder_id": "08088d6d-fe4a-4704-b265-9636d2cd750e", "file_name": "concepts-events" } }

{ "item": { "id": "5ac66235-69dc-4092-b430-9d68837e0c76", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Pipelines", "short_description": "What a pipeline is in Godzilla: a named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector through transform steps to a destination.", "body": "

Pipelines

A pipeline is the core unit of work in Godzilla: a named, versioned data-processing workflow that moves data from a source connector, through zero or more transform steps, to a destination connector. Every pipeline runs as a sequence of events flowing through that path.

Anatomy of a pipeline

Every pipeline has three parts:

  • Source — the connector that emits events into the pipeline (a database, a queue, an upload, a webhook).
  • Transforms — an ordered list of steps that reshape, filter, or enrich events as they pass through. Transforms are optional; a pipeline with none is a pass-through copy.
  • Destination — the connector that events are written to once transforms complete.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Pipelines are declarative|body_html=

You describe the desired source, transforms, and destination; Godzilla schedules and retries the runs. You never manage worker processes directly.

}}

Pipeline state

A pipeline is always in one of three states:

  • draft — configured but not yet processing events.
  • active — running on its configured schedule or trigger.
  • paused — temporarily stopped; resumes from the last checkpoint.

Versioning

Pipeline configuration is versioned. Publishing a new version does not affect events already in flight on the previous version — in-flight runs finish on the version they started on. This matters most when a pipeline definition is part of a larger migration; see the Migration guide for an example of retiring an old pipeline version safely.

Next steps

Ready to build one? Start with the Building your first pipeline guide, or jump straight to the Pipelines endpoint in the API reference.

", "version_token": "b108749e-13eb-4307-a463-7ee80904dfc5", "created_at": "2026-08-20T14:09:41.322Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-20T15:07:12.062Z", "placement_id": "90934af5-2740-4c61-ad15-b94c046ac6fe", "folder_id": "08088d6d-fe4a-4704-b265-9636d2cd750e", "file_name": "concepts-pipelines" } }

{ "item": { "id": "7418c3d6-9ea1-4d1c-8d8f-73136f6b6abb", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Connectors", "short_description": "What a connector is in Godzilla: a pre-built integration to a source or destination system, with its own auth and catalog of built-in types.", "body": "

Connectors

A connector is a pre-built integration to an external system that a Pipeline reads from or writes to. Connectors handle authentication, batching, and retry behavior for a specific system so pipeline authors don't have to.

Connector direction

  • Source — emits events into a pipeline (e.g. a change-data-capture stream from Postgres).
  • Destination — receives events from a pipeline (e.g. writing rows into Snowflake).
  • Bidirectional — a small set of connectors, like the generic Webhook connector, can act as either.

Built-in connector catalog

ConnectorDirectionAuth
PostgresSourceConnection string + replication slot
Amazon S3Source / DestinationIAM role or access key
SnowflakeDestinationKey-pair auth
KafkaSource / DestinationSASL/SSL
WebhookSource / DestinationSigned request or bearer token
{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Rotating connector credentials|body_html=

Rotating a connector's credentials pauses any pipeline using it for the duration of the rotation. Plan credential rotations outside peak processing windows.

}}

Connector health

Each connector reports a health status independent of any single pipeline: healthy, degraded, or down. A connector shared across multiple pipelines only needs to be fixed once — every pipeline referencing it recovers automatically.

See also

Connectors are configured per pipeline in the Connecting a data source guide, and referenced directly in the Connectors endpoint of the API reference.

", "version_token": "b5608109-db98-4ac0-ad46-cdcaa776847f", "created_at": "2026-08-20T14:09:49.857Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-20T15:07:12.067Z", "placement_id": "e008cc85-c171-4744-8db3-24b6237d037d", "folder_id": "08088d6d-fe4a-4704-b265-9636d2cd750e", "file_name": "concepts-connectors" } }

{ "item": { "id": "5d4595b3-af60-41b2-85ae-c325cd927db2", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Glossary", "short_description": "Definitions for Godzilla's core terms, each linking to its full explanation.", "body": "

Glossary

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Handling errors & retries.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Rate limits & errors.

args.body:
Schemas

A schema is a declarative contract that defines the expected structure, data types, and required fields for an event payload moving through a pipeline. Schemas prevent malformed records from propagating downstream and ensure data integrity across source and destination connectors.

Declaring a schema

Godzilla schemas follow standard JSON Schema (Draft-07) specifications. You define schemas per event type or attach them directly to pipeline ingress and egress stages.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=order-created.schema.json|language=json|code={ "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", "title": "OrderCreatedPayload", "type": "object", "properties": { "order_id": { "type": "string" }, "customer_id": { "type": "string" }, "amount_cents": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }, "currency": { "type": "string", "enum": ["USD", "EUR", "GBP"] }, "status": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["order_id", "amount_cents", "currency"], "additionalProperties": false }}}

Validation & enforcement modes

When a pipeline processes an event, Godzilla validates the payload against the registered schema. You can configure how validation failures are handled using one of three enforcement modes:

  • strict — Any event failing validation is immediately rejected and routed to the pipeline's dead-letter queue.
  • warn — The event continues through the pipeline, but a platform warning event is emitted for monitoring and alerting.
  • drop — Invalid events are silently discarded without halting pipeline execution or triggering retries.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Validation failure handling|body_html=

In strict mode, validation errors do not retry endlessly. Because payload schema mismatches are deterministic, failed events bypass transient retries and move straight to the dead-letter queue. See Handling errors & retries for details on inspecting and replaying dead-lettered events.

}}

Schema validation in the pipeline lifecycle

Validation can occur at three points in a pipeline run:

  1. Ingress validation — Verified immediately after a source connector emits an event, ensuring source data conforms to expectations.
  2. Post-transform validation — Verified after transform steps run to confirm reshaped payloads match target specifications.
  3. Egress validation — Checked before writing to a destination connector to guarantee downstream compatibility.

Schema evolution & compatibility

As business requirements change, schemas evolve. Godzilla supports backward and forward compatibility rules to prevent breaking active pipelines:

  • Additive changes — Adding optional fields is backward-compatible and does not require pipeline downtime.
  • Breaking changes — Removing fields or adding new required fields requires creating a new pipeline version or using a transform step to migrate payload shapes.

See also

Learn more about working with events and payloads:

  • Events concept — Structure and lifecycle of events in Godzilla.
  • Transforming events in flight — Reshape, filter, and enrich event payloads.
  • Handling errors & retries — Dead-letter queues and retry mechanisms.

args.short_description: What an event is in Godzilla: the atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.
args.body:
Events

An event is the atomic unit of data that moves through a Pipeline. Every record a source connector emits, every row a transform produces, and every write a destination connector performs is an event.

Event shape

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=event.json|language=json|code={ "id": "evt_8f2c1a90", "type": "order.created", "occurred_at": "2026-08-18T09:12:44Z", "source": "connector_postgres_orders", "payload": { "order_id": "ord_4471", "amount_cents": 4899 } }}}

Payload schemas & validation

The payload property contains the user data carried by the event. You can declare contract definitions for event payload shapes using Schemas. Godzilla validates payloads at ingress, transform, and egress boundaries to ensure data matches expected types and required attributes.

User data events vs. platform events

Godzilla distinguishes two kinds of events:

  • User data events — the records your pipelines process, shaped however your source system produces them.
  • Platform events — lifecycle notifications Godzilla itself emits: pipeline.started, pipeline.completed, pipeline.failed, connector.error. These are what power Webhooks.
{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Ordering|body_html=

Events are delivered in-order per source partition, not globally. Two events from different source partitions may be processed out of order relative to each other.

}}

Retries and dead-lettering

An event that fails a transform or destination write is retried with exponential backoff. After the configured retry limit, it is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped. See Handling errors & retries for how to configure and drain a dead-letter queue.

args.short_description: Definitions for Godzilla's core terms, each linking to its full explanation.
args.body:
Glossary

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Handling errors & retries.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Rate limits & errors.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

args.body:
Glossary

Short definitions for every term used throughout these docs.

Pipeline
A named, versioned workflow that moves data from a source connector, through optional transforms, to a destination connector.
Connector
A pre-built integration to an external system — a source, a destination, or both.
Event
The atomic unit of data moving through a pipeline, or a platform lifecycle notification like pipeline.failed.
Schema
A declarative contract specifying the structure, types, and validation rules for event payloads.
Webhook
An outbound HTTP request Godzilla sends to a URL you control when a subscribed event occurs.
Dead-letter queue
Where an event goes after exhausting its retries, rather than being dropped. See Handling errors & retries.
Cursor pagination
The pagination style used by every v2 list endpoint. See Rate limits & errors.
Workspace
The top-level account boundary an API key is scoped to.

parts.text:
I have added the **Schemas** concept page and cross-linked it across the documentation site.

### Summary of Changes
1. **Created "Schemas" Concept Page (`/concepts-schemas`)**:
   - Explains how event payload structures are declared using standard JSON Schema definitions.
   - Outlines payload validation rules and enforcement modes (`strict`, `warn`, `drop`).
   - Details pipeline validation lifecycle checkpoints (ingress, post-transform, and egress) along with compatibility and evolution guidelines.
   - Provides JSON schema examples and links to related concepts and guides (Events, Pipelines, Handling errors & retries, Transforming events in flight).

2. **Updated "Events" Concept Page (`/concepts-events`)**:
   - Added a "Payload schemas & validation" section explaining how event payloads are declared and validated against schemas, with a cross-link to the new Schemas page.
   - Fixed the dead-letter queue link to point to the current Handling Errors & Retries guide.

3. **Updated Concepts Hub (`/concepts`)**:
   - Added a concept card for **Schemas** and updated the overview copy.

4. **Updated Glossary (`/glossary`)**:
   - Added a definition entry for **Schema** linking directly to the new concept page.

### Review Links
- **Staging Preview:** https://staging.localhost:4310
- **Review URL:** http://localhost:3001/sites/32114acb-ccbe-44e4-96d4-64fa594284e2/change-sets/ea83f151-5fbc-4f00-9858-d5be59f776ff
